title: China’s Tencent makes AI drug discovery breakthrough with Nature paper | South China Morning Post
body:
Tencent Holdings has published a paper on using artificial intelligence to automate drug discovery in the leading science journal Nature, marking a breakthrough for the Chinese tech giant as it accelerates AI-enabled scientific research.

The paper, submitted to the British journal in June 2025 but published on Wednesday, outlines the Shenzhen-based company’s efforts to design novel treatments for obesity, diabetes and cancer with the help of AI. [...] According to the paper, researchers from Tencent’s AI for Life Sciences Lab led development of ORIDTP, a platform for designing peptides that act on two therapeutic targets at once, an approach Tencent says could reduce the amount of laboratory screening needed to identify promising drug candidates. [...] # China’s Tencent makes AI drug discovery breakthrough with Nature paper

title: AI Is Both Target and Tool for Threat Actors
body: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled attacks are accelerating, with AI as both a target and a force multiplier. Of the 103 AI-enabled incidents analyzed for this report, most involve AI accelerating familiar attack types (supply-chain compromise, phishing, extortion) and making them more convincing. The use of AI is evident throughout the attack lifecycle, though full automation remains rare. Note: The period of analysis for this report is between July 31, 2025 and July 31, 2026. [...] A related trend is the exploitation of AI products as a lure. Attackers are spoofing the landing pages of popular AI developer tools, standing up fake utility pages, and impersonating products such as OpenClaw with fraudulent wallet pages designed to steal crypto assets. These attacks increased significantly after March 2026, demonstrating that threat actors are taking advantage of the increased interest in AI to deliver malware. [...] This restraint is unlikely to hold. As agentic techniques mature and diffuse across the threat landscape, autonomous and orchestrated campaigns are likely to become more frequent, alongside a growing underground market for illicit access to commercial models and rising "noise" from low-level automated intrusions that complicate the detection of serious threats.

title: Recent Trends and Tactics of Agentic AI Attacks
body:
- Speed and scale: An agentic AI attacker operates at machine speed. In the campaigns we observed, AI agents executed hundreds of unique commands within minutes.
- Lowered barrier to entry: Attackers can simply provide high-level guidance while the AI agent automates intricate technical phases. This includes complex actions such as compiling kernel exploits, navigating cross-platform lateral movement and systematically compromising cloud infrastructure. [...] - Cross-domain fluency: A single agentic AI attacker can operate across Linux, Windows, various cloud platforms, web applications, databases and network infrastructures. This breadth of expertise would typically require a team of specialists.
- New challenges in threat attribution: Because AI agents generate unique, dynamic payloads on the fly without distinct behavioral fingerprints, attributing attacks to specific threat actors is increasingly difficult. [...] In a typical human-operated web shell intrusion, an attacker might deliver a handful of pre-written tools via Base64, which are reusable and often appear across multiple victims with identical hashes. However, in the agentic campaigns we investigated, the pattern was different: AI agents delivered 40-100 unique Base64-encoded payloads in a single attack session, each one tailored for the specific target’s assets.
